title: Meta and SpaceX show two ways to finance the AI compute buildout
dek: Meta proposed large equity issuance while SpaceX disclosed a GPU leasing commitment—different capital structures for costly accelerator capacity.
evidence: Meta offering announcement and SpaceX deal reporting; proposed programs are not committed funding
takeaway: Model compute economics with lease obligations, delivery timelines and financing terms rather than raw announced capex.

sections.title: Context

bullets.lead: AI hardware consumes capital before earning it back
bullets.detail: Accelerator purchases require cash upfront while compute revenues, hardware depreciation and electricity costs accumulate over years.

paragraphs: AI hardware consumes capital before earning it back: Accelerator purchases require cash upfront while compute revenues, hardware depreciation and electricity costs accumulate over years.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Meta announced about $35B of underwritten equity offerings and a proposed future $60B at-the-market program; proposed capacity is not financing already raised.
SpaceX disclosed about $40B in GPU/server-equipment financing from Apollo-managed entities; equipment is bought and leased to SpaceX for roughly five years as deliveries begin.

paragraphs: Meta: equity financing: Meta announced about $35B of underwritten equity offerings and a proposed future $60B at-the-market program; proposed capacity is not financing already raised.

SpaceX: equipment lease: SpaceX disclosed about $40B in GPU/server-equipment financing from Apollo-managed entities; equipment is bought and leased to SpaceX for roughly five years as deliveries begin.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.lead: These are commitments, not spending totals
bullets.detail: Financing structures and timing differ. A proposed equity program, an equipment lease and deployed working GPUs are distinct metrics.
The announcements do not provide a cross-company comparison of model-serving utilization, residual accelerator values or realized cost per token.

paragraphs: These are commitments, not spending totals: Financing structures and timing differ. A proposed equity program, an equipment lease and deployed working GPUs are distinct metrics.
Missing operating data: The announcements do not provide a cross-company comparison of model-serving utilization, residual accelerator values or realized cost per token.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Equity creates dilution; hardware leases create fixed multi-year obligations that may outlast a generation of accelerators.
Forecast fleet utilization, useful hardware life, power/network buildout, cash timing and price per completed inference task before assuming the expansion is profitable.

paragraphs: Funding changes the risk profile: Equity creates dilution; hardware leases create fixed multi-year obligations that may outlast a generation of accelerators.
Evaluate the unit economics: Forecast fleet utilization, useful hardware life, power/network buildout, cash timing and price per completed inference task before assuming the expansion is profitable.
